# Runner profile experiment, 2026-10-10

Keep the shared `ci` profile at ThinLTO/CGU4. ThinLTO/CGU8 did not improve these
measurements. Cargo `lto=false`/CGU4 is a promising warm-build candidate, but its
experimental binaries have not passed the native/runtime/performance gates.
Compile-time results alone do not justify adopting it. Issue #38604 remains
open for that validation and an eventual adoption decision; parent #38597 also
needs production end-to-end evidence.

The historical `off-cgu4` lane name means cross-crate LTO is disabled.
[Cargo `lto=false`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#lto)
still performs thin local LTO across a crate's codegen units; `lto="off"` would
disable LTO completely and was not measured. Baseline/CGU8 use cross-crate
`lto="thin"`. These flags, not the short lane names, define each candidate.

[Run 38076945406](https://github.com/okou-ai/okou/actions/runs/38076945406)
completed all six lanes successfully on PR head
`5198535f42392fdd28b6e7e3bedcc3fe14fc86a9`. The actual checked-out PR merge
source and CLI manifest commit were both
`2935c598f80374f12628c7f8f724a614de6d2260`.

- CLI package SHA256: `830b5f29cc215bf164677bcaf40d59771db5bdfdc29674f5c3aad7127fa6e63b`.
- CLI manifest SHA256: `894c34fba996a7c700845cee13c1082d523d8072dfe2433e3da3e4f0d5fbbea6`.
- ARM baseline input digest: `449e56a4ab9de43a3f75e72c247140dae23fe6738c8c573ea961a368c667d6dc`.
- x86 baseline input digest: `39acd08228eed5406222bdd1e1de16775cb1811b91c85157f7b4be59d4660400`.
- Container: `ghcr.io/okou-ai/vm0-toolchain-rust:20261009`; rustc 1.99.0
  (`b940084d7`), Cargo 1.99.0 (`5f94df478`), sccache 0.18.0, mold 2.41.0,
  Python 3.12.3. Actual executable and instrumentation hashes are in each manifest.
- Each independent lane reported eight CPUs/eight-CPU affinity, AMD EPYC 9V45,
  approximately 31.34 GiB physical memory, and cpuset `0-7`. Container CPU/memory
  limits were `max`. These are six separate VMs, not paired runs on one host.
- All identity fields match within each target except the explicit profile
  overrides. Across targets only the expected target, baseline input digest,
  target linker and profile override differ.
- The `ci` profile inherits release optimization/stripping, with ThinLTO/CGU4
  overridden only in each experimental process. Release remains LTO=true/CGU1;
  the local profile remains unchanged. Both musl targets retain mold/static flags.
- Registry sources were prefetched outside the timed commands. Each lane used
  an empty 4 GiB job-local disk sccache for one seed, then retained it for three
  warm trials. The complete Cargo output directory was deleted at the same path
  before every trial. This does not model production R2 or restored Cargo outputs.

The six diagnostic artifacts retain manifests, phase/resource/cache JSON,
per-invocation linker JSON, output hashes/sizes and Cargo timing HTML. Artifact
retention is seven days; the observations below remain in this dated report.

## Wall-time observations

Seconds, with all warm samples shown in execution order. Each median is over
three observations. Total is the median of each trial's guest-plus-runner sum,
not the sum of two independently calculated medians.

| Target | Profile | Cold guest / runner, n=1 | Warm guest, n=3 | Warm runner, n=3 | Warm total median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 70.43 / 169.69 | 26.65, 28.16, 29.00 | 106.00, 107.63, 109.04 | 135.80 |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 80.03 / 181.40 | 30.37, 30.32, 29.60 | 114.10, 111.62, 110.18 | 141.94 |
| ARM | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 64.54 / 179.65 | 13.36, 12.98, 13.20 | 76.32, 77.65, 76.47 | 89.68 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 68.47 / 170.93 | 28.78, 27.19, 27.00 | 106.93, 104.47, 102.07 | 131.66 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 62.23 / 166.22 | 30.91, 31.21, 29.05 | 106.22, 105.03, 106.17 | 136.24 |
| x86 | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 62.02 / 182.25 | 14.18, 13.86, 13.89 | 76.46, 75.73, 73.45 | 89.59 |

`lto=false` reduced the warm guest median by 53.1% (ARM) / 48.9% (x86), the runner
median by 29.0% / 27.5%, and the combined median by 34.0% / 32.0%. CGU8 increased
the combined median by 4.5% / 3.5%. The single cold runner observation was slower
with `lto=false` on both targets; it does not establish a cold regression or gain.

## Supported attribution and resource observations

Cargo reports the following warm unit durations. Units overlap and must not be
summed to reconstruct the phase wall time. The external linker is the existing
musl GCC/mold driver invocation for the runner output, not rustc's LTO work.

| Target | Profile | Runner compiler unit range, s | Kerberos build.rs range, s | Runner external linker range, s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 57.87–58.86 | 41.93–45.80 | 0.147–0.150 |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 62.25–63.96 | 42.62–44.64 | 0.207–0.213 |
| ARM | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 26.99–27.85 | 43.38–44.75 | 0.129–0.132 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 54.97–56.96 | 41.69–44.29 | 0.127–0.140 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 58.24–60.96 | 39.81–41.54 | 0.175–0.178 |
| x86 | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 25.76–26.83 | 42.33–44.17 | 0.108–0.114 |

The root compiler unit becomes shorter when cross-crate LTO is disabled, while the native
Kerberos build script still takes about 40–46 seconds. That script fetches and
verifies pinned Zig/Kerberos sources into its Cargo output, extracts/configures
them, builds native libraries and packages the worker. Clearing Cargo outputs
also clears those downloads/native caches. Its interval includes network and
native build work; this experiment does not separately time those operations.
Other native dependency build scripts also recur. Neither the historical
82-second runner phase nor this experiment's 100-second baseline is all linking.

[Cargo's timing documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/timings.html)
explains that binary units do not show when code generation starts. The measured
root binaries have no frontend/codegen section split, although some library
units do. Frontend, codegen, ThinLTO, payload processing and IO within the root
compiler unit remain unseparated; external driver time cannot identify them.

Runner-phase resource observations below are medians over the same three warm
trials. Container CPU includes the local sccache server. Child CPU is also
recorded in raw JSON but excludes work delegated to that server.

| Target | Profile | Container CPU, s | Maximum child RSS, GiB | Sampled container memory maximum, GiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 527.09 | 2.82 | 7.29 |
| ARM | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 590.32 | 2.81 | 7.25 |
| ARM | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 220.63 | 1.97 | 5.85 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU4 | 503.74 | 2.34 | 6.88 |
| x86 | ThinLTO/CGU8 | 551.33 | 2.20 | 6.71 |
| x86 | `lto=false`/CGU4 | 215.37 | 1.99 | 5.79 |

Maximum child RSS is a process high-water mark, not aggregate memory. Container
memory is sampled every 100 ms, includes the resident cache, and is not a reset
kernel `memory.peak` measurement. These values do not prove memory savings.

All warm guest/runner trials had zero cache misses; uncacheable requests still
numbered 54/55 on ARM and 54/56 on x86. x86 guest trials also recorded two C/C++
cache errors consistently across all profiles, so a hits/(hits+misses) value of
100% must not be described as an error-free or fully cached build. The error
cause is not established by these reports. Raw counters also record two guest
and one runner compiler failures despite every Cargo command succeeding; those
counters cannot be interpreted as failed benchmark jobs.

## CI overhead, compatibility and decision

The CLI job took 31 seconds, including a 13-second package build. Lane container
initialization took 19–21 seconds, checkout 3–7 seconds, artifact download
1–2 seconds and immutable-input verification at most one second at GitHub's
timestamp resolution. The complete measurement step, including materialization,
registry prefetch, seed and three warm rebuilds, took 537–712 seconds. Queue time
and those setup costs are outside the measured guest/runner commands. These
lanes do not demonstrate required-check or production end-to-end improvements.

Shared-profile callers were audited: canonical runner compile, local
`dev-runner.sh` guest/runner builds, the `guest_rpc` native test artifact and its
profile assertions, and documented native builds. Experimental overrides stay
inside these lanes; release callers and native helper recipes retain their
existing flags. All four required gates passed on the measured PR head, but
they exercised canonical profiles, not the six diagnostic binary outputs.

Do not adopt CGU8 from this evidence. Preserve ThinLTO/CGU4 for this PR. Validate
`lto=false` in a separate change against unchanged architecture, behavior, runtime,
performance, transport and compiler-contract gates before any shared-profile
change. Retain full candidate flags in every binary/cache identity if that
follow-up publishes or reuses different bytes. Three sequential warm trials
per lane cannot establish P95, cross-run reproducibility or production savings.
